subject: Termination for Convenience: handback schedule & notice-tier proposal
messages:
From: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@novushealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@novushealth.com, Jason Miller <jason.miller@novushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novus draft: termination for convenience / data handback

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for sending over the latest order form (attached). Our legal team flagged Section 6 — Term; Renewal; and Termination — specifically the TFC language and the lack of a concrete handback schedule. Two asks from our side before we can route this to procurement: 

1) Clarify auto-renew mechanics (term length and opt-out notice window).
2) Define a clear data handback SLA and a practical timeline by dataset size — we need predictability for clinical data exports.

I've attached Novus' standard requests to the email (see Data_Handback_SLA.pdf) and highlighted a preference for a 60-day opt-out notice for annual terms. Can you propose how Redwood would handle a TFC termination (fees, transition support, and a calendar for returning data)?

Regards,
Elena
Director, Strategic Ops
Novus Health

Attachments: Novus_Data_Handback_SLA_Request.pdf

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, contracts@novushealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus draft: termination for convenience / data handback

Elena — thanks for the clear note and the SLA doc. We're aligned on the need for a concrete handback plan. High level proposal from Redwood: 

- Term & Auto-renew: 12-month initial term with a 60-day opt-out window before renewal (we can support a 30-day window only for pilots under $50k TCV).
- Termination for Convenience (TFC): either party may terminate with 90 days' notice; if Customer terminates for convenience, no termination fee; if Redwood terminates for convenience (rare), we propose a prorated refund for unused prepaid committed capacity plus 60 days of transition support.
- Data handback: tiered timeline based on dataset size: 
  * Small (<100GB): 30 days after effective termination
  * Medium (100GB-1TB): 60 days
  * Large (>1TB): 90 days + optional staged export (customer pays reasonable egress if >5TB)
- Transition support: included 60 hours of engineering assistance for handback for all tiers; additional time is billable at our professional services rates.

I'll loop in Marissa (contracts) and Karthik (legal liaison) for redlines to the Order Form. Attaching a proposed clause snippet shortly.

Best,
Mateo
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@novushealth.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, contracts@novushealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus draft: termination for convenience / data handback

Elena — quick note from commercial/legal on the practical redline approach: 

1) Auto-renew mechanics: we'll accept a 12-month term with 60-day opt-out for standard customers. For enterprise deals where Novus needs longer notice for procurement alignment, we can agree to a 90-day opt-out as long as the order form includes the purchase order cadence and a payment holdback clause.

2) TFC fee structure: Mateo's proposal stands for customer-initiated TFC (no fee). For Redwood-initiated TFC, we'll provide a prorated refund plus a 30-day wind-down credit unless the termination is for cause. We want to avoid open-ended credits.

3) Data handback SLA: Redwood proposes the tiered schedule above. Two operational clarifications requested from Novus: 
  - How will Novus consume exports? (S3 bucket vs. physical transfer)
  - Do they require verified deletion certificates?

4) We recommend adding a 'staggered notice' paragraph: if Novus reduces committed capacity >25% within a 3-month window, we treat that as a material change and trigger a 30-day operational planning period. This protects both parties during large scale unwinds.

Could Novus confirm consumption method and whether deletion certs are required? If so, we'll bake in a deletion-cert process and a 5% holdback on final invoice until verified.

Thanks — looping Karthik for legal redlines.

Marissa
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: contracts@novushealth.com, Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus draft: termination for convenience / data handback

Elena / Novus team — thanks for the handshake. A couple of legal clarifications and proposed language: 

A) Notice windows: we propose the following carved language for the Order Form: "Either party may provide written notice to terminate this Order Form for convenience. For Order Forms with an annual term, Customer must provide written notice at least sixty (60) days prior to the then-current Term Expiration to opt-out of renewal. For pilots or trials under $50,000 TCV, Customer may provide thirty (30) days' notice."

B) Data handback and egress: "Upon termination, Redwood will provide Customer with exported data in a mutually agreed format. Export timelines shall be tiered by Customer dataset size as defined in the Order Form. Redwood will not be liable for egress charges incurred by Customer on third-party storage; such charges will be passed through unless otherwise agreed."

C) Termination for Convenience (commercial): "If Customer terminates for convenience, Redwood will provide the data handback and transition support as set forth herein and will not assess a termination fee. If Redwood terminates for convenience, Redwood will provide a pro rata credit for prepaid fees plus thirty (30) days' transition assistance. Each party's maximum liability for transition costs caused by a termination for convenience shall be limited to the greater of $100,000 or the fees paid for the prior three (3) months."

D) Verification & deletion: "Upon completion of data handback, Customer may request a Certificate of Deletion. Redwood will provide such certificate within thirty (30) days of Customer's written request, subject to any lawful data retention obligations."

If Novus confirms the consumption method (S3 preferred) and whether certificates are required, we can prepare a redline of the Order Form with the precise clauses.

Karthik
Legal Counsel — Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@novushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@novushealth.com, Jason Miller <jason.miller@novushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus draft: termination for convenience / data handback

Team — appreciate the speed. Novus confirms: 

- Consumption method: S3 (us-east-1) preferred, with encryption maintained in transit.
- Deletion certificates: required for regulated data; we'll include the template language in our next email.
- We accept the tiered handback timeline and the 60-day opt-out for annual terms. For Redwood-initiated TFC, Novus requests a 60-day transition (not 30), given clinical safety reviews — is that acceptable?

Action items:
- Redwood to send a redline of the Order Form with the agreed TFC + handback clauses (Marissa / Karthik) — target EOD Monday.
- Novus to send deletion-cert template and confirm S3 bucket details — target Monday morning.

Elena
Director, Strategic Ops
Novus Health
